summary: Fence a backtest's paid provider calls against a superseded lease (#1464): catalog.IdempotencyKeyed / catalog.SupportsIdempotencyKey let a call node declare that its provider deduplicates a repeated CallInput.IdempotencyKey, and catalog.RequestKeyer names the canonical request a call sends; engine.DryRunInput.Fence (engine.CallFence) gives every real call a stable key (scope, node, its graph.CallSite — token and visit, from the new graph.DryRunOptions.ExecuteAt — and a digest of the request sent: RequestKey, else DecisionKey, else params and step context; never the lease), checks the holder right before each call and, when strict, refuses providers that cannot deduplicate, and requests with no stable form, with engine.ErrUnfenced; backtest examples run under a lease fence, and backtest.Config.StrictFencing (off by default) refuses paid backtests over such providers. The residual risk without strict fencing is documented: the calls a superseded worker made in an unfinished example may be paid again when the next worker replays it.
